params.body:
Three things on the Insights screen, all of them visible the moment you open it.

## The groove was empty

The series drew a correct vertical axis next to a box of two hundred pixels with nothing in it.

Since the axis arrived, `.act-groef` is a flex item beside the labels, and a flex item does not grow by itself. It shrank to its content, and that content is bars carrying `flex: 1 1 0`, which collapse to nothing without a basis. So: a perfect axis, and no bars to measure against it.

```css
.act-groef { position: relative; overflow: visible; flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; }
```

`min-width: 0` belongs with it: without it the smallest content size of a flex item blocks the shrink as soon as there are many bars.

I checked the source, the compiled view and the served CSS after the previous merge and concluded there was nothing to fix. There was; it was simply invisible until this rule existed.

## The rail under the tabs was the colour of the page

`#eaecf0` on a page background of `#edf1f5`. The rail disappeared and the blue marker floated under the word as a loose bar, which reads as a rendering fault rather than as a tab. It is now `#d0d5dd`, the same grey the rest of the screen uses for a border.

## The tabs did not say what they hold

"De zaak" and "Activiteit" are not a pair: one carries an article and the other does not, "activiteit" can as easily mean how busy the servers are as how much work the people did, and neither says what you get when you click.

A tab name is all the reader has before choosing. They now name the question behind them, in all four languages:

| | nl | en | fr | de |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | Klanten en omzet | Customers and turnover | Clients et chiffre | Kunden und Umsatz |
| | Gebruik | Usage | Utilisation | Nutzung |

The key in the URL stays `activiteit`. It sits in bookmarks and in the redirect from `/activity` (R P3-16.10), and a URL that travels with a label breaks every link anyone ever shared.

## Verified

Two tests added to `ABarYouCanReadANumberOffTest` for the groove and the rail, both of which would otherwise fail silently: CSS that does nothing renders without an error. One added to `ActivityScreenTest` for the tab names, which also pins that the URL key did not move with them and that all four languages carry both labels.

New rule R P3-16.16. While there: the em dash that slipped into R P3-16.15 yesterday is gone.

`npm run build` green, `phpstan` green. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment; CI runs against a fresh database.
params.title: Let the groove fill its row, and name the tabs after their question
